label: TSMM to A2A Protocol binding
description: Maps A2A protocol concepts to TSMM agent interaction and v0.19.0 discovery, capability negotiation, task evidence, observability, and opacity governance abstractions.

mappings.description: Public Agent Card maps to ServiceDescriptor with disclosurePolicy: public. Authenticity binding is optional at this tier.
Authenticated extended Agent Card maps to ServiceDescriptor with disclosurePolicy: authenticated. authenticityBinding is required.
A2A Skill maps to SkillContract. inputModes, outputModes, and tags map directly. authorizationScope is added by TSMM as the governance layer A2A does not explicitly model.

A2A contextId groups tasks and messages. TSMM InteractionContext adds inheritedAuthorityRefs, inheritedEvidenceRefs, and reAuthorizationPolicy — the governance semantics contextId implies but does not formalize.

A2A Task maps to InteractionTask. TSMM adds explicit governance significance to each status transition, authorizationCheckpointRef for paused tasks, and cancellationReason as a governance-required field.

A2A input-required task state maps to InteractionTask (status: input-required) with an active AuthorizationCheckpoint (triggerCondition: input-required). TSMM treats this as a governance checkpoint, not a transport wait state.

A2A auth-required task state maps to InteractionTask (status: auth-required) with an AuthorizationCheckpoint (triggerCondition: auth-required or scope-exceeded). TSMM models the authority boundary event explicitly.
A2A extension mechanism maps to ExtensionContract. requiredness, negotiatedStatus, and failureHandling capture the negotiation record. resolutionRecord is added by TSMM for audit purposes.

A2A's foundational design principle — agents collaborate without exposing internal state, memory, or tools — is not a protocol element in A2A but has direct governance consequences. TSMM models it as a structural governance constraint with explicit evidenceGap and trustScopeConstraint.

A2A assumes agents interact as peers with no hierarchical relationship. TSMM formalizes this as PeerTrustRelation with explicit trustBasis and trustScope — governance structure A2A implies but does not model.

A2A's Message, Artifact, and Part model the wire payload structure. TSMM does not mirror the wire model; it models the governance obligations governing payload content by modality via ContentProvenancePolicy.

A2A SSE streaming maps to ObservabilityMode (deliveryModel: streaming). TSMM models governance consequences: auditabilityLevel: partial, replayRisk: low, required compensating controls for sequence gaps and clean-close confirmation.

A2A push notification maps to ObservabilityMode (deliveryModel: push-callback). Governance consequence: userAwarenessModel: delayed or opaque; replayRisk: medium from retries; idempotency keys required as compensating control.

A2A security schemes declared in the Agent Card map to a two-layer TSMM model: declared posture in ServiceDescriptor.authenticityBinding, runtime enforcement through SkillContract.authorizationScope, and checkpoint-raising via AuthorizationCheckpoint when authentication requirements are unmet.
Well-known URI, curated registry, direct configuration, authenticated extended card, and restricted catalog discovery map to TSMM discoveryMode values.
Descriptor freshness, cache TTL, ETag expectation, revalidation, and failure behavior are explicit TSMM governance properties.

mappings.externalConcept: Authenticated extended Agent Card access control
mappings.description: TSMM treats extended-card access as a governed disclosure decision requiring access policy, integrity, and evidence references.
Missing required extensions must cause rejection or review in the TSMM capability negotiation model.
TSMM maps task state transitions to evidence obligations for authorization, completion, rejection, failure, and cancellation.
Delivery models are mapped to auditability, replay risk, user awareness, and compensating control expectations.

notes: TSMM generalizes A2A mechanics into governance semantics; this is not an A2A conformance claim.
v0.19.0 adds descriptor discovery, capability negotiation, and task lifecycle evidence surfaces.

guarantees.name: governed-discovery-and-negotiation
guarantees.description: A2A discovery, capability negotiation, and task-lifecycle events can be represented as TSMM governance artifacts.

guarantees.name: runtime-authority-completeness
guarantees.description: TSMM can record runtime authorization checkpoints, but A2A transport conformance alone does not establish the authority, policy, or evidence required for a permitted effect.

limitations.name: protocol-conformance-separation
limitations.impact: This semantic binding does not certify A2A protocol conformance or the legitimacy of a discovered agent.
limitations.mitigation: Validate A2A behavior separately and bind discovery, policy, authority, and evidence to each trust decision.

behavioralExpectations.expectation: Consumers MUST evaluate descriptor integrity, freshness, and disclosure policy before relying on advertised capabilities.
A privileged task continuation SHOULD produce an authorization checkpoint and decision evidence before an operational effect occurs.

notes: Suitable for architecture, validation, and assurance design; not an A2A conformance claim.
